differences.what: the camera: re-anchored from the conservatory's (fitted on the ground, the stable and the drum), it draws the house about 7% larger than the print (the 18th Street face's two corners 321 px apart against the print's 301, x 131 and 432) and 10-20 px east; the readings below are made at the scale those two corners give. A gap two camera fits disagree about (T-3153)

the owner's report, 2026-10-30, on this print: the rear (east) face 'stepped'. The print reads it in two sections, the south one (x 432-477 px) with one light a storey and one dormer and the north one (x 495-560) with two lights a storey and two dormers, divided by a lit, banded return under a hip in the mansard (x 477-495); the build's rear was one flat face under one mansard. Built: the north section (v 0-11.48) stands 0.9 m out under its own mansard and cornice, banded pilasters at its corners, the raised terrace in the angle (p_rear; the depth reconstructed, L-pullman-1729-rear-step-1881)

the rear face's lights and dormers: the print's one light a storey on the south section (x about 457, v about 14.7) and one dormer over it (x about 450), and two lights a storey on the north section (x about 512 and 545, v 7.7 and 2.9) with a dormer over each (x 503-512 and 537-548); the build had two lights and two dormers at v 14.93 and 10.93. Now one and one at v 14.93, and two and two on p_rear at v 8.04 and 3.44, set symmetric on the section (within about 0.5 m of the print's)

the step's depth: the lit return's 18 px (with the corner pilaster's face) are drawn by a 0.9 m step at the 18th Street face's scale; the corners alone hold 0.5-1.8 m. Under this camera's overcast light the build's return reads the same tone as the faces either side of it, where the print's is lit

the porte-cochere on the 18th Street flank (x 206-252 px): the print draws a block standing before the flank with a deep, dark arch and its own cornice and balcony at y 475-480; through this camera the render draws its arches (x about 143-214) as shallow recesses in the flank's plane, without the block's shadowed returns. Its form and place were worked against Taylor's no. 1445, which sees it squarely; whether the gap here is the camera's scale and offset or the block's depth is not read
differences.how: T-1881 (2026-11-06), read by projecting the build's porte_cochere through this camera and by two diagnostic renders (no flora, sun): the block stands 5.97 m out from the flank in the GLB (a render from u -5, v 42 shows it whole, its balustraded top, its east arch and its front arch). From this eye, south-east of it, the block's EAST END faces the camera more squarely than its front: the east arch's centre projects to x 237, y 511, inside the print's dark arch (x 206-252), and the render's ring at x 215-250 is that arch; the ring at x 143-214 the record compared before is the front arch, foreshortened (its centre at x 176). So the arch the print draws is where the build has it, within about 8 px. What differs is tone: the print's block and its arch read dark, and the review render draws the block's faces, its opening and the flank behind it in one stone under the overcast key with no occlusion, so the block's returns do not separate from the flank. The house's heights through this camera run about 20-40 px off the print's (the cornice at the corner projects at y 382 where the print's is about 420), as the solve says (fitted on the ground and the stable, the house's corner 28 px off), so the block's heights are carried by Taylor's no. 1445, which sees its west arch square at 18-20 px a metre through a camera fitted on the house, and matches there.

differences.what: the parkway and lawn trees: the print's are slender trees with fine crowns; the render draws the app's winter trees as a few coarse limbs, thicker, and not at the print's places. As in the house's other three views [T-1881, 2026-11-03: the house's own 18th Street trees west of this stretch (3.7, 14.25 and 24.65 m) now grow on `high_head`, a tall leader under a narrow head off the Detroit print and Taylor's no. 1445; through this camera they stand beside the house's flank as straight boles with their heads from about the second storey, nearer the print's slender trees than the forked crowns they replace; the print's trees still stand at other places, so this stays open]

the 18th Street boundary in the foreground (x 100-560): the print, of the early 1890s, shows the earlier wall with its piers and urns and the low walls sweeping between them; the build is the wall as the Detroit view of about 1900 shows it, nearest 1 July 1904 (the boundary's note, L-pullman-18th-street-wall-c1900-1934), so this print cannot show the 1904 wall
colour and the ivy: the print is monochrome and of winter, with no leaf on the walls
the mansard's cresting: the print's is taller and finialled at each hip (y 315-330 px); the build's is plain iron about 0.8 m high round the deck and the sections
differences.how: T-1881 (2026-11-01): read at the print's full size against the mansard's 4.0 m rise (curb y 334, cornice y 398 at the pier by the south-east hip, about 16 px a metre): the pierced band stands about 17 px (1.05 m) over the curb and the tall post at that hip about 28 px (1.75 m), about 4 px (0.25 m) across, a turned finial on top; the Detroit print shows the same posts over the curb at each section's hips (x about 317, 381, 416, 501 and 585 px) rising about 2 m over a band about 1 m deep. Built: the cresting on the deck and on each pavilion's own curb raised from 0.8 to 1.0 m (the kit's most, between the two readings), and a turned iron finial 1.75 m high, 0.12 m in radius, on every hip: each pavilion's two (a new K01 mansard-bay key, roof.mansard.cresting.finials) and the main deck's four corners (mansard.deck.finials). The render now draws a finialled post at each hip it sees, the cresting run between. The posts' places through this camera carry its known offset on the house (the scale item below); the darker plain upright at x about 363 px is not read as a finial (it stands off any hip and reads like a stack's pot) and is not built. The finials' turning is the deck kit's, not read (L-pullman-1729-hip-finials-1881).

differences.what: the main block's height through this camera: the cornice at the south-east corner at y about 394 px and the deck's cresting at about 325 in the print, against about 358 and 300 in the render, which is the camera's scale (above), not a storey

a stack rising behind the house's rear face, between its two dormers (x 512-523 px, its cap at about y 317, about 4 px over the cresting), which the build did not stand (seen first in the conservatory's record of this picture) [T-1881, 2026-11-07: placed through the Detroit print det 4a08066, whose camera is fitted on the rear face's corners and dormers: the stack now stands on the deck at v 4.6, between the rear step's two dormers (v 8.04 and 3.44), where T-1934 had set it at v 10.0 against this print's dormers. Through this camera, which draws the rear about 20-30 px right of the print's, it renders at x about 528-538 over the step's south dormer against the print's 512-523: the camera's offset, not the stack's place]
differences.how: T-1934 (2026-11-03): built as the house's fourth stack (chimneys.stacks[3], u 1.4, v 10.0, top 18.4 m), placed against the rear face's dormers since this camera is not fitted on the house's rear: it now renders between the first and second rear dormers, about a fifth to a third of the way (x 486-494 against the dormers' 476 and 540), where the print sets it 0.35 of the way (512-523 against 500 and 543); the whole rear renders about 25 px left of the print's through this camera, as the house's other items here say. L-pullman-1729-rear-stack-1934

differences.what: T-3429 (2026-11-06): the parkway elms are bare round wood now, twig forking off twig, where T-1934's painted twig cards stood; read against the print again, the verdict is kept.

[T-1881, 2026-11-07] a second dark, capped stack behind the cresting at x about 428-442 px (its top near y 305), left of the south section's dormer: the Detroit print det 4a08066 shows the same stack over the south section's dormer, and it is built from that print at (1.4, 13.5), top 18.4 m; through this camera it renders at x about 455-465, the camera's 20-30 px offset along the rear

the 18th Street flank's ground-storey lights east of the porte-cochere: this winter print, of the early 1890s, draws narrow round-headed lights under the pavilion's triple and in the east section, where the build now has two broad square-headed windows under transoms, read off the Detroit print det 4a08066 of c. 1900 (T-1881, 2026-11-07); two dated pictures disagree and the later one governs a 1904 build, so the earlier lights are read as altered before c. 1900

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
